title: Setback to a communal street: no provision in Table 3.3a
text: C3.3.1 Buildings are set back from the street boundary in accordance with Table 3.3a. Table 3.3a Minimum setback of buildings from the street, street type: Primary street; Secondary street; Adjoining laneway or right-of-way, where it is not the primary street to the dwelling; Adjoining laneway or right-of-way where it is the primary street to the dwelling (1). (1) Does not apply to ancillary dwellings.

replaces.note: 'Adjoining communal street 0.5 m' row not carried
2.5 m (1.5 m porch) where a grouped dwelling not adjacent to the primary street has its main frontage to a communal street

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: No value is encoded. Neither Table 3.3a (p30) nor Table 3A (p7) has a communal street row, although 'street' includes a communal street, the Table of Changes says setbacks to communal streets are reduced, Figure 3.3d (p32) still shows a 2.5 m communal street setback citing Part B, and Figure 3.7g refers to the 'street setback to communal street (Table 3.3a)'. A dwelling fronting its own communal street could be read as needing the primary or secondary street value, or the 0.5 m right-of-way value; a planner decides until clarified (register ch3-047, highest priority for 2-5 dwelling infill). The Part C 0.5 m value is not applied. Fact building.communal_street_setback_m is recorded for the planner.

verified.note: Confirmed missing: Table 3.3a (p30) has four street-type rows and no communal street row; Table 3A (p7) has none either. Figure 3.3d (p32) still shows a '2.5m communal street setback (clause 5.1.2 C2.1 iv)' and a '1.5m communal street setback (Table B column 7 secondary street)'. The page gives no value, so the rule stays judgment.
